correctness.rationale: A PSD covariance factor B supplies finite row vectors. Their convex-hull distance squared is precisely the simplex covariance minimum. Orthogonal projection gives a unit vector with every loading at least sqrt(m); this is valid even when Sigma is singular. Conditioning on orthogonal Gaussian residuals leaves all coordinate transforms increasing in the same independent scalar normal, implying nonnegative conditional pair covariances. An explicit Hermite-series computation controls each conditional-mean variance by the square of the residual correlation; hence conditional variance is at least (a_i^2/Sigma_ii) times marginal variance. Total variance yields beta >= m/max diag. A nonnegative null vector, when m=0, makes the monotone linear sum zero with positive denominator. The ancillary verifier checks exact examples and finite forms; no infinite claim relies on numerics.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves an explicitly posed Gaussian distribution-copositivity conjecture for all finite-dimensional singular covariance matrices, yields a computable nontrivial covariance-only coercivity certificate, and exhibits a singular covariance with a non-matching four-edge negative-correlation graph. Its proof combines convex geometry, conditional covariance order and Gaussian Hermite contraction, addressing a motivated structural gap rather than an arbitrary finite calculation. It does not claim sharpness of the bound or general non-Gaussian extensions.
